challenge.exploration_summary: I explored the Helmet codebase and its test suite. The project is a collection of small, focused security-header middlewares written in TypeScript and tested with node:test. The Content-Security-Policy middleware is one of the most complex modules, already supports dynamic directive-value functions, and is exported both standalone and through the top-level helmet wrapper. It is a natural place to add a helper for CSP nonces, which are a common real-world need.
challenge.feature_spec: Add a contentSecurityPolicy.nonce() helper that returns a per-request directive-value function. Each call generates a cryptographically random base64url nonce, stores the raw nonce on res.locals.cspNonce so templates can use it, and returns the properly quoted 'nonce-<value>' source expression for use in CSP directives.
challenge.feature_rationale: CSP nonces are the recommended way to allow inline scripts/styles without weakening a policy. Generating them correctly (cryptographically random, base64url, quoted) and surfacing the raw nonce to the response object is boilerplate that Helmet can provide. Because the CSP middleware already accepts functions as directive values, a nonce helper integrates cleanly without changing existing behavior.
challenge.bug_description: The nonce() helper generates the raw nonce once when the helper is invoked, then reuses that same nonce for every subsequent request handled by the returned function. CSP nonces must be unique per request; reusing a nonce across requests allows an attacker who can inject markup (e.g., via a stored-HTML bug or reflected payload) to reuse a known nonce and bypass the policy's protection against inline scripts/styles.

findings.description: The PR inserted the `nonce` property declaration inside the call-signature return type of the `ContentSecurityPolicy` interface instead of as a top-level property. This produces invalid TypeScript and prevents the project from compiling.

The `generateNonce`, `nonce`, and helper declarations were placed inside `getHeaderValue`, making them local to that function. As a result `contentSecurityPolicy.nonce` at module scope cannot reference them, again breaking compilation and scoping the feature incorrectly.

The nonce is generated once when `contentSecurityPolicy.nonce()` is called and then reused from the closure for every request. If a user creates the helper once at module load and reuses it across requests (the natural way to use a directive-value function), all visitors receive the same static nonce, completely defeating the purpose of CSP nonces and allowing bypass of the policy.

self_review.fix_explanation: I rewrote the nonce implementation so that: (1) the `nonce` property is correctly declared as a top-level member of the `ContentSecurityPolicy` interface, (2) the nonce helper functions are defined at module scope instead of being nested inside `getHeaderValue`, and (3) the random nonce is generated per request inside the returned directive-value function, while still reusing the same raw nonce stored on `res.locals.cspNonce` within a single request. This ensures unique per-request nonces even when the helper is created once and reused across requests, preserves the same nonce across multiple CSP directives in one response, and keeps all existing and new tests passing.
